sentences.en: You may have seen a Noguchi table.
sentences.zh: 你可能见过野口勇茶几。

sentences.en: Actually, I know you've seen it.

sentences.zh: 它就像是咖啡桌的代名词。

sentences.en: In movies or TV shows, when they want to show that a lawyer or an art dealer is really sophisticated,
sentences.zh: 在电影或电视剧里，当他们想表现一位律师或艺术品商人的品位非常高雅时，

sentences.en: they put a Noguchi table in their waiting room.
sentences.zh: 他们会在候客室里放上一张野口勇茶几。

sentences.en: And it is really a beautiful table.
sentences.zh: 而且这确实是一张很美的桌子。

sentences.en: Two curvy wooden legs interlock and support this heavy slab of glass,
sentences.zh: 两根曲线优美的木腿相互交错，支撑着厚重的玻璃板，

sentences.en: which seems like it's almost floating above them.
sentences.zh: 看起来就像漂浮在上方一样。

sentences.en: Since the Noguchi coffee table was introduced in 1948,
sentences.zh: 自1948年野口勇咖啡桌问世以来，

sentences.en: it's become one of the emblems of mid-century industrial design.
sentences.zh: 它已成为世纪中期工业设计的标志之一。

sentences.en: It has its own Wikipedia page, and there's a thriving Instagram hashtag,
sentences.zh: 它有自己的维基百科页面，还有一个非常火的Instagram标签，

sentences.en: hashtag FYNCT, which stands for F*** Your Noguchi Coffee Table,
sentences.zh: 标签是FYNCT，意思是“去你的野口勇咖啡桌”，

sentences.en: which basically means F*** Your Bougie Cliché Interiors.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是在说“去你的那些虚伪做作的室内装潢”。

sentences.en: Which is ironic because, like all eventual clichés,
sentences.zh: 这很讽刺，因为像所有最终沦为陈词滥调的事物一样，
野口勇本人曾是非常前卫的。

sentences.en: And he was so much more than that.
Choreographers and fashion designers and art directors,
sentences.zh: 编舞家、时装设计师、艺术总监，

sentences.en: and, you know, a whole lot of different people across a really wide creative swath
sentences.zh: 还有很多来自不同创意领域的人，

sentences.en: look to Noguchi as a point of inspiration.
sentences.zh: 都将野口勇视为灵感来源。

sentences.en: This is Dakin Hart, senior curator of the Isamu Noguchi Foundation and Garden Museum.
sentences.zh: 这是达金·哈特，野口勇基金会暨庭园美术馆的资深策展人。

sentences.en: Noguchi himself built this studio in Queens to house a lifetime of his abstract,
sentences.zh: 野口勇亲自在皇后区建造了这个工作室，用来存放他一生中那些抽象的、

sentences.en: evocative experiments in stone and metal.
sentences.zh: 引人深思的石材与金属实验作品。

sentences.en: Hart says Noguchi was challenging himself with every sculpture.
sentences.zh: 哈特说，野口勇在每一件雕塑作品中都在挑战自我。

sentences.en: Can I make something hard feel soft?
sentences.zh: 我能让坚硬的东西感觉柔软吗？

sentences.en: Can I make something heavy feel light?
sentences.zh: 我能让沉重的东西感觉轻盈吗？

sentences.en: Can I make something far away feel like it's right next to you?
sentences.zh: 我能让遥远的东西感觉近在咫尺吗？

sentences.en: You know, to make rock feel fluid that way.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是让岩石产生那种流动的质感。

sentences.en: Noguchi's sculptures seem to twist and balance on themselves,
sentences.zh: 野口勇的雕塑似乎在自身之上扭转并保持平衡，
随着形态和纹理起伏波动。

sentences.en: But this is all his later work.
sentences.zh: 但这都是他后期的作品。

sentences.en: Back in the 1930s, before Noguchi had a signature museum and a namesake coffee table,
sentences.zh: 回到20世纪30年代，在野口勇拥有专属美术馆和同名咖啡桌之前，

sentences.en: he was a struggling artist in New York City.
sentences.zh: 他只是纽约市一名挣扎求生的艺术家。

sentences.en: He paid the bills by sculpting busts of rich people.
sentences.zh: 他靠为富人雕刻半身像来维持生计。

sentences.en: He called it head-busting, and he did it just to make money.
sentences.zh: 他称之为“砸头”，他做这个纯粹是为了赚钱。

sentences.en: Or he said he did it just to make money.
sentences.zh: 或者说，他自称是为了赚钱。

sentences.en: But in truth, he used it brilliantly as a way to social network.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，他巧妙地利用这一点作为社交手段。

sentences.en: And it was a way to romance the people who were his patrons.
sentences.zh: 这也是一种与他的赞助人建立亲密关系的方式。

sentences.en: Noguchi was as great a networker as he was a sculptor.
sentences.zh: 野口勇不仅是一位伟大的雕塑家，也是一位出色的社交家。
但“砸头”并不能带来成就感。
他想思考更宏大的东西。

sentences.en: Here's Noguchi in an interview from the 70s.
sentences.zh: 这是野口勇70年代接受采访时的片段。

sentences.en: Noguchi wanted to make art that would live in the world,
sentences.zh: 野口勇想创作出能融入世界的艺术，

sentences.en: not just in a rich person's home or on a gallery wall.
sentences.zh: 而不仅仅是放在富人的家里或画廊的墙上。

sentences.en: He wanted to change the physical landscape that people moved through.
sentences.zh: 他想改变人们所处的物理景观。

sentences.en: Noguchi said that he wanted people to feel like the first person on Earth.
sentences.zh: 野口勇说，他希望人们感觉自己像是地球上的第一个人。

sentences.en: The first person to explore Earth.
And so he started to think of a concept for a giant public sculpture.
sentences.zh: 于是，他开始构思一个巨大的公共雕塑概念。

sentences.en: It looked like a massive, massive pyramid.
sentences.zh: 它看起来像是一座巨大无比的金字塔。

sentences.en: Imagine a cross between a Mayan temple and a mountain,
sentences.zh: 想象一下玛雅神庙和山峰的结合体，

sentences.en: pushing up out of the Earth with a long slide sloping down it
sentences.zh: 从大地中拔地而起，一侧有长长的滑梯倾斜而下，

sentences.en: and steps on two of its faces.
It is a step pyramid, essentially.
sentences.zh: 本质上，它是一座阶梯金字塔。

sentences.en: But on each side, the steps are different heights.
sentences.zh: 但在每一侧，台阶的高度都不同。

sentences.en: But it wasn't just a sculpture for a museum or a bank plaza.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅是为美术馆或银行广场设计的雕塑。

sentences.en: Noguchi thought of it as a playground.
sentences.zh: 野口勇把它看作一个游乐场。

sentences.en: So he talked about play as the primer for a purposeful approach to space.
sentences.zh: 他谈到将游戏作为一种有目的的空间探索方式的入门。

sentences.en: Trying to teach people to be more mindful of space and how we occupy it and how it works.
sentences.zh: 试图教导人们更加关注空间，关注我们如何占据空间以及它是如何运作的。

sentences.en: This giant ziggurat wouldn't come with any specific instructions.
sentences.zh: 这座巨大的塔庙不会附带任何具体的使用说明。

sentences.en: It would have no rules, no single obvious way to play with it.
sentences.zh: 它没有规则，没有单一明显的游玩方式。

sentences.en: Noguchi wanted Play Mountain to be a strange new landscape
sentences.zh: 野口勇希望“游乐山”成为一种奇特的新景观，

sentences.en: that would dare children to imagine other realities
sentences.zh: 能够激发孩子们去想象其他的现实，

sentences.en: so that perhaps they could grow up into creative, open-minded adults.
sentences.zh: 这样他们或许能成长为富有创造力、思想开明的成年人。

sentences.en: And I think Noguchi hoped that by making playgrounds,
sentences.zh: 我想野口勇希望通过建造游乐场，

sentences.en: he could impact people at that key stage in development.
sentences.zh: 能在人们发展的关键阶段产生影响。

sentences.en: In fact, the inspiration for Play Mountain came to Noguchi
sentences.zh: 事实上，“游乐山”的灵感来源于野口勇

sentences.en: when he was at this key stage himself, when he was a little boy.
sentences.zh: 在他自己处于这个关键阶段时，也就是他还是个小男孩的时候。

sentences.en: Isamu Noguchi was born in Los Angeles in 1904.
sentences.zh: 野口勇于1904年出生在洛杉矶。

sentences.en: His father Yone was a famous Japanese poet,
sentences.zh: 他的父亲米良是一位著名的日本诗人，

sentences.en: and his mother was a white American writer named Leonie Gilmore.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲是一位名叫莱奥妮·吉尔摩的美国白人作家。

sentences.en: They met when she answered an ad he placed in the paper for a translator and assistant.
sentences.zh: 他们相识于她应聘了他刊登在报纸上的翻译兼助理广告。

sentences.en: Pretty much as soon as Isamu was born,
sentences.zh: 几乎在野口勇出生后不久，

sentences.en: Yone abandoned them and went back to Japan.
sentences.zh: 米良就抛弃了他们回到了日本。

sentences.en: Noguchi and his mother eventually followed,
sentences.zh: 野口勇和母亲后来也跟了过去，

sentences.en: but his father had already started another family by then.
sentences.zh: 但那时他的父亲已经组建了另一个家庭。

sentences.en: So Noguchi and his mother moved to a countryside town
sentences.zh: 于是野口勇和母亲搬到了一个乡村小镇，

sentences.en: where Noguchi's bright blue eyes marked him as an outsider to the other kids at school.
sentences.zh: 在那里，野口勇明亮的蓝眼睛让他成了学校里其他孩子眼中的异类。

sentences.en: But from their little house in the little town they lived in on the seaside,
sentences.zh: 但从他们居住的海边小镇的小房子里，

sentences.en: they did have a great view of Mount Fuji,
sentences.zh: 他们确实能看到富士山的绝佳景色，

sentences.en: but Fuji quite far away, so like just the perfect little pyramid.
sentences.zh: 但富士山离得很远，看起来就像一座完美的小金字塔。

sentences.en: So you can imagine that view that this little boy has every day going down the stairs seeing Mount Fuji.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象，这个小男孩每天走下楼梯看到富士山时的那种景象。

sentences.en: That idea of his own Mount Fuji stuck with Noguchi.
sentences.zh: 那种属于他自己的富士山的概念深深印在了野口勇心中。

sentences.en: It followed him when he moved to Indiana as a teenager.
sentences.zh: 当他十几岁搬到印第安纳州时，这个念头一直伴随着他。

sentences.en: It followed him to Paris where he apprenticed with the sculptor Brancusi.
sentences.zh: 当他去巴黎师从雕塑家布朗库西时，它也跟着他。

sentences.en: And it came with him to New York City, the place that he decided would become his home.
sentences.zh: 它还随他来到了纽约市，那个他决定安家的地方。

sentences.en: So it was like, imagine taking Mount Fuji and turning it into a giant play structure.
sentences.zh: 所以就像是，想象一下把富士山变成一个巨大的游乐设施。

sentences.en: I think that's what Play Mountain was.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是“游乐山”的意义所在。

sentences.en: Play Mountain was my response based upon memory of my own unhappy childhood,
sentences.zh: “游乐山”是我基于自己不幸童年的记忆所做出的回应，

sentences.en: the desolate playground on a cliff in Tokyo which I approached with dread.
sentences.zh: 那是一个位于东京悬崖上的荒凉游乐场，我曾怀着恐惧接近它。

sentences.en: It may be that this is how I tried to join the city, New York, to belong.
sentences.zh: 也许这就是我试图融入纽约这座城市，试图找到归属感的方式。

sentences.en: Noguchi wanted to move the mountain from his lonely childhood
sentences.zh: 野口勇想把童年孤独记忆中的那座山搬过来，

sentences.en: and reincarnate it as a place for gathering and playing,
sentences.zh: 并将其重塑为一个聚集和玩耍的地方，

sentences.en: as a kind of gift to the children of New York.
sentences.zh: 作为送给纽约孩子们的一份礼物。

sentences.en: And after years and years of carrying that concept in his head,
sentences.zh: 在脑海中酝酿了这个概念多年之后，

sentences.en: In 1934, one of the fancy people Noguchi had made a bust of
sentences.zh: 1934年，野口勇曾为其雕刻过半身像的一位名流，

sentences.en: helped him get a meeting with Robert Moses,
sentences.zh: 帮他争取到了与罗伯特·摩西会面的机会，

sentences.en: the newly appointed commissioner of the New York City Parks Department.
sentences.zh: 摩西是新上任的纽约市公园管理局局长。

sentences.en: Moses had said his number one priority was to build more playgrounds in the city,
sentences.zh: 摩西曾表示，他的首要任务是在城市里建造更多的游乐场，

sentences.en: which at the time had very few.
sentences.zh: 当时纽约的游乐场非常少。

sentences.en: So Noguchi decided to bring him his idea.
sentences.zh: 于是野口勇决定带上他的想法去见他。

sentences.en: Noguchi brought Moses a model of Play Mountain,
sentences.zh: 野口勇带给摩西一个“游乐山”的模型，

sentences.en: two feet square, made of white plaster on a wooden frame,
sentences.zh: 两英尺见方，用木架上的白色石膏制成，

sentences.en: designed to take up an entire New York City block.
sentences.zh: 设计规模足以占据整个纽约街区。

sentences.en: Noguchi carries this miniature mountain to Robert Moses' office
sentences.zh: 野口勇带着这座微型山来到罗伯特·摩西的办公室，

sentences.en: and dunks it down on Robert Moses' desk.
sentences.zh: 把它重重地放在了罗伯特·摩西的桌子上。

sentences.en: And says, what if we, you know, we build this for the children of the city?
sentences.zh: 然后说，如果我们为城市里的孩子们建造这个怎么样？

sentences.en: This is Alexandra Lang, architecture critic at Curbed
sentences.zh: 这是亚历山德拉·朗，Curbed网站的建筑评论家，

sentences.en: and author of The Design of Childhood.
sentences.zh: 也是《童年设计》一书的作者。

sentences.en: And Moses is like, no way.
The playgrounds Moses envisioned were simple.
sentences.zh: 摩西设想的游乐场很简单。

sentences.en: Asphalt or dirt surrounded by a chain-link fence
sentences.zh: 沥青或泥地，周围围着铁丝网，

sentences.en: with the four S's of playground equipment.
sentences.zh: 配有游乐场设备的“四个S”：

sentences.en: Moses was planning just to plonk these four S's in vacant lots
sentences.zh: 摩西计划在全市的空地上大量铺设这“四个S”，

sentences.en: all over the city, by the hundreds.
And here comes Noguchi with this massive, ambiguous,
sentences.zh: 而野口勇却带着这个巨大的、模糊的、
超凡脱俗的城市山丘来了，

sentences.en: which would have required the movement of huge amounts of earth and concrete
sentences.zh: 这需要搬运大量的土方和混凝土，

sentences.en: and probably would have cost a ton of money.
sentences.zh: 而且可能要花一大笔钱。

sentences.en: And he just laughed his head off and threw us out, more or less.
sentences.zh: 他只是大笑了一场，差不多就把我们赶了出来。

sentences.en: Like, four S's, I'm just going to order them,
sentences.zh: 就像是，四个S，我直接订购就行了，

sentences.en: and, like, we're going to have, you know, 400 playgrounds by tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，明天我们就能有400个游乐场了。

sentences.en: Robert Moses did end up erecting 658 playgrounds in New York
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·摩西最终确实在纽约建造了658个游乐场，

sentences.en: But from this moment on, he and Noguchi became lifelong enemies.
sentences.zh: 但从那一刻起，他和野口勇成了终身的敌人。

sentences.en: He took his model and went home, fuming.
sentences.zh: 他带着模型回家了，气愤不已。

sentences.en: And he fumed about it for the rest of his life, really.
sentences.zh: 他余生都在为此愤愤不平，真的。

sentences.en: The concept of Play Mountain remained very close to Noguchi's heart.
sentences.zh: “游乐山”的概念在野口勇心中一直占据着非常重要的位置。

sentences.en: Play Mountain was the kernel out of which have grown
sentences.zh: “游乐山”是我所有关于雕塑与大地关系的构想的内核，

sentences.en: all my ideas relating sculpture to the earth.
sentences.zh: 它们都是从这里生长出来的。

sentences.en: Play Mountain represented this idea that Noguchi had,
sentences.zh: “游乐山”代表了野口勇的一个理念，

sentences.en: that children didn't need instructions to play.
sentences.zh: 即孩子们玩耍并不需要说明书。

sentences.en: With, say, swings or a slide,
there's only one way to use them,
sentences.zh: 它们只有一种使用方式，

sentences.en: and kids just do the same prescribed activities over and over again.
sentences.zh: 孩子们只会一遍又一遍地重复同样的规定动作。

sentences.en: But if you give children an abstract, surreal landscape,
sentences.zh: 但如果你给孩子们一个抽象的、超现实的景观，

sentences.en: they can interpret it however they want.
sentences.zh: 他们可以随心所欲地去解读。

sentences.en: They can make up stories and have adventures
sentences.zh: 他们可以编造故事，展开冒险，

sentences.en: and use their intuition to play in a thousand different ways.
sentences.zh: 并运用直觉，以千百种不同的方式去玩耍。

sentences.en: This philosophy would later be called non-directive play.
sentences.zh: 这种理念后来被称为“非指导性游戏”。

sentences.en: For Noguchi, this was the way that sculpture could be out in the world
sentences.zh: 对野口勇来说，这就是雕塑走向世界的方式，

sentences.en: and really change the way people move and think.
sentences.zh: 并能真正改变人们的行动和思维方式。

sentences.en: He wasn't going to give up on it so easily.
sentences.zh: 他并不打算轻易放弃这个想法。

sentences.en: In 1939, Noguchi offered to design a playground for Honolulu's A La Moana Park.
sentences.zh: 1939年，野口勇提议为檀香山的阿拉莫阿纳公园设计一个游乐场。

sentences.en: Still not discouraged, Noguchi pitches his Hawaii playground ideas
sentences.zh: 野口勇并未气馁，他再次向纽约公园管理局

sentences.en: back to the New York Parks Department, again.
sentences.zh: 推销他在夏威夷的游乐场构想。

sentences.en: And so Noguchi, still excited by the challenge,
sentences.zh: 于是，依然对挑战充满热情的野口勇，

sentences.en: went off and designed Contoured Playground.
sentences.zh: 转而设计了“轮廓游乐场”。
它本质上是一个平滑、抽象的景观，

sentences.en: of sloping hills and dales and riverbeds.
sentences.zh: 有着起伏的丘陵、山谷和河床。

sentences.en: It's still a non-directive playground, but it's very subtle.
sentences.zh: 这仍然是一个非指导性的游乐场，但手法非常微妙。

sentences.en: This time, the New York Parks Department actually seems open to it.
sentences.zh: 这一次，纽约公园管理局似乎真的对此持开放态度。

sentences.en: They even start talking about finding a spot in Central Park to build it.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至开始讨论在中央公园找个地方来建造它。

sentences.en: But by then, the year was 1941.
And Noguchi's plans were about to change.
sentences.zh: 野口勇的计划即将发生改变。

sentences.en: Noguchi was in California visiting a friend.
sentences.zh: 当时野口勇正在加州探望一位朋友。

sentences.en: And he was out shopping for some onyx for a sculpture.
sentences.zh: 他正外出为一件雕塑选购缟玛瑙。

sentences.en: In fact, I was on my way to San Diego.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我当时正在去圣地亚哥的路上。

sentences.en: And I happened to turn on the radio, and that's where I heard it.
sentences.zh: 我碰巧打开了收音机，就在那里听到了消息。

sentences.en: We interrupt this program to bring you a special news bulletin.
sentences.zh: 我们中断节目，为您播报一则特别新闻简报。

sentences.en: The Japanese have attacked Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, by air.
sentences.zh: 日本人已从空中袭击了夏威夷珍珠港。
罗斯福总统刚刚宣布了这一消息。

sentences.en: oh, well, oh my God, I'm a Japanese.
Or I'm a Nisei, at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 或者至少，我是个日裔美国人。

sentences.en: Nisei are Americans born to Japanese parents.
sentences.zh: 日裔美国人是指出生于日本父母的美国人。

sentences.en: by both the Parks Department and Noguchi.
